\title{Strain-stabilized skyrmions in thin magnetic films}
\author{A. Author}
\affiliation{Institute, City}

\begin{abstract}
Magnetic skyrmions are candidates for dense memory.
Here we predict that strain widens the skyrmion stability window in thin films by a factor of 2.6 at room temperature.
\end{abstract}

\maketitle

Spin-orbit torque (SOT) moves skyrmions~\cite{a,b}.
SOT also moves domain walls, and SOT efficiency depends on the interface.
Figure~\ref{fig:one} shows the geometry, and Fig.~\ref{fig:two} shows the stability window.
The energy density is
\begin{equation}
E = A (\nabla \mathbf{m})^2 ,
\label{eq:energy}
\end{equation}
where $A$ is the exchange stiffness.
The window grows by a factor of 2.6, as Eq.~\eqref{eq:energy} implies.
